Cardiomegaly is absent because the heart silhouette is of normal size and shape. The cardiothoracic ratio, which is the ratio of the widest part of the heart to the widest part of the inner rib cage, is within the normal limit of less than 0.5.
Atelectasis is absent as there are no linear bands of increased density or signs of volume loss that would suggest a collapse of any part of the lungs.
Lung Lesion is absent because no focal masses or nodules are visible within the lung parenchyma or the hilar regions.
Pleural Effusion is absent as the costophrenic and cardiophrenic angles on both sides are sharp and clearly defined, showing no evidence of fluid accumulation in the pleural space.
Fracture is absent since the visible skeletal structures, including the ribs, clavicles, and spine, show no signs of cortical break or displacement.
